AbstractText.Label: CONTEXT
AbstractText.content: Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis (IPF) is a progressive, incurable interstitial lung disease with heavy symptom burden and poor quality of life. The last year of life is characterized by increased acute care utilization and hospital deaths. Clinical guidelines recommend early integration of palliative care but is rarely implemented. In 2012, we reorganized our clinic into a multidisciplinary team comprising two pulmonologists (expertise in ILD and palliative respiratory care respectively), nurse, respiratory therapist, physiotherapist, and a dietitian. We adopted an early integrated palliative approach with a focus on early symptom management and advance care planning starting at the first clinic visit. We designed a Multidisciplinary Collaborative (MDC) care model with emphasis on community-based care to manage patients in their homes and support caregivers.

AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVES
AbstractText.content: Exploratory analysis of this model's association with acute care utilization in the last year of life and location of death was undertaken.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: Data from deceased IPF patients pre-and post 2012 (non-MDC & MDC care model respectively) was collected and statistical analysis was performed.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: Patients in MDC care were 24.2 times less likely to have respiratory-related ER visits (95%CI, 3.12, 187.44, p=0.002), 2.32 times less likely to have respiratory-related hospitalizations (95%CI, 0.95, 5.6, p=0.064). The odds of achieving a home or hospice death in MDC care were 9.2 times compared to non-MDC care, who die mostly in the hospital (95%CI 1.14, 75, p=0.037).

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSIONS
AbstractText.content: MDC care model for IPF was associated with reduced healthcare use in the last year of life and more home deaths.
